Salmo 118

Beáti immaculáti

Draft 18, Sunday Prime — reviewed. Pray it aloud first; then decide below. Every choice you make rewrites the psalm here, so what you pray is what you chose. Nothing is final until you say so.

Dotted gold marks words still waiting for your decision — touch one to choose its wording where it stands. A gold wash marks where your choice departs from draft 18.

Each verse from the Latin down to what is prayed. Between one draft and the next, words that left are struck through and words that came carry the gold wash; beside them, who objected and what the audit says. A verse no draft touched folds to one line — open it to see its strata.

The literal tier: the Latin’s words and order kept as far as Portuguese grammar allows — the scaffold the prayed text was made from, not a text to pray.

Word by word: under each Latin word, its lemma’s dictionary sense and its form. Generated, not translated — LatinCy’s parse, unreviewed, and one gloss per lemma (interlinear/); … marks a gloss not yet written, and a dotted word a lemma rare in the psalter. Under each verse, the prayed text as you have chosen it. tense.mood.voice.person-number for verbs; case.number.gender for nouns, adjectives, participles; the indicative, the active and a noun’s gender go unsaid. nom gen dat acc abl voc cases · sg pl singular, plural · m f n masculine, feminine, neuter · 1s 2s 3s 1p 2p 3p person and number (acc.1s = me) · pres impf fut perf plqp futp present, imperfect, future, perfect, pluperfect, future perfect · subj imp subjunctive, imperative · pass passive (LatinCy parses most deponents so) · inf part ger gdv sup infinitive, participle, gerund, gerundive, supine · comp superl comparative, superlative · conj. prep. adv. interj. neg. num. n.pr. the words that do not inflect, and proper names

The audit trail

1source

Latin = DO Psalm118.txt, 176 prayed verses, each with one '*' and no other mark; this file holds 118:1–118:32 only (stanzas Aleph–Daleth, the portion of Sunday Prime) and later agents append. The Hetzenauer 1914 print read of the Latin was skipped overnight and is owed.

2word study

Before any verse: words/ps118-terms.md — the law-vocabulary counted from the Latin (ps118/terms.py → terms.md), the Greek behind each term, Lewis & Short, what Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal Monástico did (ps118/renderings.py → renderings.md), and a ruling under the night's delegation: lex → lei, testimónia → testemunhos, mandáta → mandamentos, justificatiónes → preceitos, judícia → juízos, verbum → palavra, sermo → fala, elóquium → dito, via → caminho, sémita → vereda. Each term with a live alternative is one multi-slot glossary decision here. ps118/verbs.py lists the recurring verbs; ps118/concordances.sh regenerates the words/ concordances; ps118/cnbb_tally.py is diction evidence only.

3draft

Stanza-level draft from consult/parallels/ps118.md. DO's Portuguese was not used as evidence (D12). Latin against the Greek, Latin followed: 118:9 córrigit present (Greek future); 118:17 vivífica me imperative (Greek 'I shall live'); 118:20 justificatiónes (Greek κρίματα); 118:28 dormitávit (Rahlfs ἔσταξεν). Rule 3 checked at every imperative: ensinai, dai, vivificai, desvendai, tirai, fazei, confirmai, afastai, tende are safe; 'retribuí' (118:17) and 'instruí' (118:27) fail and were recast. Register held plain on purpose: no variation added to the Latin's own.

4checks

PARTIAL hard check. checks.py cannot run on a partial psalm (it stops at the first untranslated verse), so ps118/partial.py runs checks.py's own code, unchanged, with the Latin restricted to the verses translated, after confirming that the 32 ids are an unbroken run of DO's ids from 118:1 in DO's order; 118:33–118:176 are missing, as expected. For the 32 verses: ids and marks match (one '*' each, nothing else). Soft flags, all accepted: six cola run 3–6 short and every one of them holds 'preceitos' (3 syllables for the 7 of justificatiónes: 118:5, 8, 16, 20, 23, 24) — the price of the term, psalm-wide; six run 3–5 long: 118:1 (Bem-aventurados, glossary), 118:4 (mandamentos + the passive clause), 118:6 (não serei confundido), 118:15 (mandamentos + me exercitarei), 118:29, 118:32 (quando dilatastes o meu coração) — nothing is added in any of them. Neighbouring finals: 118:16/17 (falas / falas) and 118:23/24 (preceitos / preceitos) are the Latin's own repetitions (sermónes tuos twice; justificatiónibus tuis / justificatiónes tuæ). No rhyme inside a verse, no cadence flag. A first run showed a doubled 'aos aos' in 118:31 from two overlapping slots, and 118:17 at +4 with 'Dai retribuição ao'; both mended before any reader saw the text.

5latinist

Draft 1 (prayed.v1.vos.json; latin.json trimmed to the 32 verses by ps118/partial.py). Two minor remarks, nothing major; marks confirmed in all 32 verses.

gpt-6-astra · 2026-09-21 · critic/v1.latinist.json · read prayed.vos.json

27

minor

“Fazei-me entender o caminho dos vossos preceitos” Viam justificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me

«Instrue me» pede instrução. «Fazei-me entender» é defensável como resultado dessa instrução, mas desloca o pedido para a compreensão.

proposedInstruí-me no caminho dos vossos preceitos

kept as an option under Viam justificatiónum tuárum ínstrue me — Rule 3: under vós 'instruí' is also 'I instructed'. 'Fazei-me entender' is the Greek verb exactly (συνετίζω) and Douay-Rheims' rendering.

31

minor

“não me deixeis confundido” noli me confúndere

O latim pede diretamente que Deus não confunda o orante. «Deixar confundido» pode ter sentido causativo, mas também introduz a leitura de permitir ou manter esse estado.

proposednão me confundais

❧ taken — Taken as to the construction — draft 2 has the direct 'não me envergonheis'; the verb itself changed because of the ambiguity reader.

Os 32 versículos preservam substancialmente o sentido do latim, inclusive suas construções peculiares; encontrei apenas dois pontos menores de precisão. Todos os sinais de apontamento coincidem com os do latim em identidade e ordem.

6stylist

Draft 1. Nine verses remarked; best line 118:19, worst 118:20. Six taken (grammar, order, or a plainer faithful word); 'falas' refused three times and kept as the text, with 'palavras' as the option.

gpt-6-astra · 2026-09-21 · critic/v1.stylist.json · read prayed.vos.json

5

fails: native

“se dirijam os meus caminhos, * para guardar”

A construção faz ouvir os caminhos como sujeitos de «guardar». A intenção da oração demora a ficar clara.

proposedOxalá os meus caminhos sejam dirigidos, * para que eu guarde os vossos preceitos!

❧ taken

9

fails: native

“Com que corrige o jovem o seu caminho? / as vossas falas”

A pergunta acumula inversões; «falas» soa como referência a intervenções numa conversa ou num espetáculo.

proposedComo o jovem corrige o seu caminho? * Guardando as vossas palavras.

❧ taken — The order is taken. 'Como' is refused (in quo is 'by what'; option in 'in_quo'). 'palavras' is refused: see 118:16.

10

fails: native

“não me rejeiteis dos vossos mandamentos”

«Rejeitar dos» não tem regência natural em português. O ouvido precisa reconstruir a ideia de afastamento.

proposedDe todo o meu coração vos procurei: * não me afasteis dos vossos mandamentos.

❧ taken

16

fails: native

“as vossas falas”

«Falas» traz uma associação com diálogo ou discurso que destoa da oração. «Palavras» conserva o sentido com maior naturalidade.

proposedNos vossos preceitos meditarei: * não esquecerei as vossas palavras.

❧ taken — taken in draft 3 by the main session (D15)

17

fails: native

“guardarei as vossas falas”

A combinação de «guardar» com «falas» soa fabricada. A repetição de sermónes pede a mesma solução adotada nos outros versos.

proposedRecompensai o vosso servo, vivificai-me: * e guardarei as vossas palavras:

❧ taken — taken in draft 3 by the main session (D15)

20

fails: native

“cobiçou desejar”

«Cobiçar» seguido de infinitivo soa pouco português e sugere desejo de posse. O duplo movimento do desejo deve permanecer, mas pode ganhar uma construção mais natural.

proposedA minha alma ansiou por desejar os vossos preceitos, * em todo tempo.

❧ taken

22

fails: plain

“o opróbrio”

É uma palavra que muitos reconhecerão como solene sem reconhecer de imediato o sentido. A oração perde transparência.

proposedTirai de mim a desonra e o desprezo: * porque procurei os vossos testemunhos.

❧ taken — Taken as to the fault; the word chosen is 'afronta' (it gives exprobráre its verb), 'desonra' is an option.

23

fails: sayable

“o vosso servo, porém, exercitava-se”

O inciso entre pausas interrompe um membro já comprido; a sequência até «exercitava-se» exige uma retomada pouco fluida.

proposedPois os príncipes se sentaram e falavam contra mim: * mas o vosso servo se exercitava nos vossos preceitos.

❧ taken

24

fails: native

“e o meu conselho, os vossos preceitos”

A inversão com o verbo omitido parece uma enumeração quando ouvida. O vínculo entre conselho e preceitos só se esclarece depois.

proposedPois também os vossos testemunhos são a minha meditação: * e os vossos preceitos são o meu conselho.

❧ taken

O salmo tem sobriedade e uma voz de oração bastante estável; as repetições sustentam bem a recitação. Os tropeços concentram-se em algumas construções calcadas no latim e em escolhas de vocabulário que chamam atenção para si. As terminações atendem à cadência pedida, sem rimas insistentes entre a mediante e o final.

worst line118:20

best line118:19

7ambiguity

Draft 1, Portuguese only. 45 items and 18 'unknown words' (8 distinct: sondam, iniquidade, preceitos, fitar, deleitei, vivificai-me, opróbrio, dormitou — a severe list). One real fault: 'confundido' heard as 'confused' in both its verses → the verb changed. Two that confirmed the stylist (118:10, 118:22). The rest are the Latin's own openness or were heard rightly first.

O salmo tem sobriedade e uma repetição dos possessivos que sustenta bem a oração; as imagens dos caminhos, das mãos e do coração têm presença na voz. A fluência perde força sobretudo em «vosso dito» e em algumas construções calcadas no latim, enquanto o primeiro cólon de 118:78 pesa no fôlego. As terminações são quase todas adequadas à cadência pedida, sem rimas insistentes entre os dois membros.

22stylist

Read draft 6 of 118:33–80, blind. Of the six places of the singular it now passes four — the formula in 118:41 and 118:58, 118:67, and 118:76, where its own proposed line keeps “segundo o que dissestes ao vosso servo” — and objects in two, both about the order around the clause, not the clause: 118:38 (“firmai o que dissestes para” blurs who the saying is for) and 118:50 (“porque o que” stacks unstressed words). Both mended by order alone: 118:38 dative first, “Firmai para o vosso servo o que dissestes”; 118:50 verb first, “porque me vivificou o que dissestes”. Its ten other remarks fall on verses the translating agent had already weighed after the first stylist pass (118:33, 44, 46, 57, 60, 65, 70, 75, 76a, 78); they were NOT acted on in this revision and are left in the critic file for review — none concerns a law-term.

23draft

Draft 7 = draft 6 (118:1–80, untouched, kept as prayed.v6.json) + the first draft of 118:81–128 (Caph–Ain), by the third Ps 118 agent. From the Latin, read with the Rahlfs Greek, Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares 1932 (pdftotext layer in consult/parallels/ps118.md); the Diurnal Monástico 1962 for diction only; DO's Portuguese not consulted as a witness (D12). Lewis & Short looked up for consummátio, fabulátio (it cites this very verse: "narration, discourse"), confígo, fauces, calúmnior (letter F fetched into consult/). D15/D16 vocabulary applied throughout by adding slots to the existing term decisions (justificationes, testimonia, mandata, judicia, eloquia, confundi, vivifica, supersperavi, exquirere, scrutantur, semita, legem_pone, intellectum, humilitate); 43 new verse-local decisions. Places where the Latin goes with the Septuagint against the Hebrew, all followed: 118:83 frost (not smoke), 118:85 tales told (not pits dug), 118:109 my hands, 118:112 "for the reward", 118:113 the iniquitous (not the double-minded), 118:119 "I reckoned as transgressors" (not dross), 118:120 "pierce … with your fear", 118:121–122 slander (not oppression), 118:126 the vocative Dómine, 118:127 topaz. Hard readings: defícere in (118:81, 82, 123); elóquium after a preposition (118:82) and with a genitive (118:123); consummavérunt / consummatiónis (118:87, 96); Voluntária … beneplácita fac (118:108); Tempus faciéndi (118:126). Rule-3 trap met: "Agi" (fac cum, 118:124) → "Tratai". The Hetzenauer print read is owed for these verses as for the rest.

24checks

Draft 7, via ps118/partial.py: hard checks pass (128 of 176 verses, ids and marks match). Two rhymes at mediant and final that the Latin does not have were removed by order alone before any reader saw the draft (118:92 meditação / humilhação; 118:102 apartei / lei). Accepted: neighbouring finals 118:111 / 118:112 (coração / retribuição — a suffix rhyme; both words are fixed by the glossary and each closes a one-phrase colon); and inside 118:111 "a exultação do meu coração" (exsultátio cordis mei — no other order is Portuguese). Length: long cola are nearly all "os vossos mandamentos" (accepted psalm-wide) or "pus toda a esperança" (118:81, 114; the decision of 118:43); 118:96b is +6 ("o vosso mandamento é amplo sobremaneira" for latum mandátum tuum nimis) against a first colon of −3 — the short option "é muito amplo" is in decision "latum96"; 118:95a +4 for the unmistakable "para me fazer perecer". Short cola (118:83b, 94b, 117b, −4/−5) are where "os vossos preceitos" stands for the seven syllables of justificatiónes tuas. 118:111 opens on "Adquiri", a first-person past that equals the vós imperative of adquirir: the reverse of rule 3's trap; left, because "acquire your testimonies by inheritance" is no sentence anyone would hear addressed to God.

27ambiguity

Read the Portuguese of 118:81–128 alone (ps118/part3/blind/). 49 entries; most hear the verse rightly or find the Latin's own openness (118:84 the days, 118:85 the ellipsis, 118:96 finem, 118:112 retribuição, 118:126 who is to act). Wrong first hearings, and what was done: 118:82 "pelo que dissestes" as cause → the preposition changed in all three verses of defícere in; 118:85 "fábulas" as moral tales → "histórias"; 118:97 "todo o dia" as "every day" → "o dia todo"; 118:115 "malignos" as demons → "malvados"; 118:82 "dizendo" attached to the speaker, not the eyes → kept, with the finite verb as an option; 118:109 the soul in my hands heard as control rather than danger → kept (the Latin's image, unexplained). On D16: the clause was understood in 118:116; in 118:82 the mishearing was the preposition's doing, not the clause's (the reader's right reading was "waiting for the fulfilment of what you said"); "o dito da vossa justiça" (118:123) was understood at once. The law-words were heard as in the earlier portions (testemunhos as declarations given by God, four times; juízos as norms first, sentences second). Unknown words listed: odre, preceitos (six times), iníquos / iniquamente / iniquidade, vivificai-me, sobremaneira (now gone), veredas, exultação, Traspassai, topázio.

Draft 8 = 118:81–128 revised after the three readers; 118:1–80 untouched (ps118/verify_untouched_v6.py). Changed verses: 118:81, 82, 123 (defícere in → à espera de); 85 (histórias); 90 (copula); 92 (rebuilt); 95 (destruir); 96 (order; muito amplo); 97 (o dia todo); 98–100 (natural order); 103 (order); 106 (resolvi); 107 (de todo humilhado); 108 (Fazei que vos agradem); 111, 112 (adverb moved); 113, 128 (tive ódio, the Latin's order); 115 (malvados); 116 (no que aguardo); 125 (conheça); 128 (me dirigia para). New decisions: dicentes, tota_die, usq107, maligni. Held under D16 against the stylist: "os vossos ditos" (118:103), "o dito da vossa justiça" (118:123). Held against the Latinist (minor): "o meu auxílio e o meu amparo" (118:114). Because the wording changed materially, the Latinist gate is run again on this draft.

29latinist

The gate on draft 8, 118:81–128 only. Two findings, both major; every other verse "adequate to the Latin", marks identical. 118:128 dirigébar is passive — taken (draft 9). 118:114 abstract nouns for adjútor / suscéptor — the draft-7 remark again, raised from minor to major with the text unchanged — held on purpose. None of draft 8's new wordings drew a remark: "à espera de" for defícere in (118:81, 82, 123), "histórias" (85), the rebuilt 118:92, "destruir" (95), "muito amplo" (96), the natural order of 98–100, "resolvi" (106), "Fazei que vos agradem" (108), "tive ódio" (113, 128), "malvados" (115), "no que aguardo" (116), "conheça" (125); nor the D16 clause or "dito".

Lewis & Short looked up for declarátio, áttraho, tabésco, adulescéntulus, matúritas, dilúculum, formído, erúcto, postulátio, scándalum, nimis, éxitus — it cites three of these verses itself (118:130 declarátio, 118:165 scándalum, 118:170 postulátio). Verse lists checked with ps005/grep_latin.py. D15/D16/D23 vocabulary applied by adding slots to the existing term decisions (justificationes, testimonia, mandata, judicia, sermones, eloquia, scrutantur, exquirere, mandasti, vivifica, intellectum, supersperavi, in_aeternum, humilitate, praevaricantes, odio_habui, exspectare, fiat, concupivit, adjuva, erravi); 38 new verse-local decisions. elóquium: nine places (plural 118:148, 158, 162; singular 118:133, 140, 154, 169, 170, 172), the clause in all six singulars — none forced a noun. in ætérnum → para sempre at 118:142, 144, 152, 160 (D23). Where the Latin goes its own way against the Greek it is followed: 118:139 zelus meus (not "of your house"), 118:148 ad te, 118:151 viæ tuæ (not "commandments"), 118:154 elóquium (Greek λόγον), 118:156 misericórdiæ (Greek οἰκτιρμοί); and one slip in a witness: Douay-Rheims repeats "mercy" in 118:149b where the Latin has judícium. Variations the Latin makes inside one Greek word: merged where Portuguese has no plain pair (requíram with exquírere → procurar), kept where it has one (custodívit / Servávi → guardou / Observei; Inítio / Princípium → início / princípio; juxta / secúndum → conforme / segundo). Rule-3 traps met: "Dirigi" (118:133 → Endireitai), "Redimi-me" / "Remi-me" (also "I redeemed myself" → Resgatai-me), "Ouvi" (118:149 → Escutai, as the glossary row directs). Hard readings: 118:138 (double accusative), 118:131 attráxi spíritum, 118:136 Éxitus aquárum deduxérunt, 118:140 Ignítum, 118:147 in maturitáte, 118:176 quæ périit (perecer would make a dead sheep). The Hetzenauer print read is owed for these verses as for the rest.

Mended before any reader saw the draft: 118:163 rhyme at mediant and final (abominei / lei) → both verbs first, decision "v163a"; 118:174 / 175 neighbouring finals (meditação / auxiliarão) → the verb moved before its subject in 118:175; 118:176a +5 → "como ovelha" without the article (+3); 118:141 both cola −4 → "muito jovem" (the diminutive said). Accepted: 118:154 "resgatai-me … vivificai-me" at mediant and final — the Latin has the same echo (rédime me … vivífica me), rule 5's exception. Long cola (+3/+4) are the psalm-wide cost of "os vossos mandamentos" and of the formulas (118:134b = 146b, 147b "pus toda a esperança", 151b, 168b, 172b) or a verb of motion with its complement (118:148a "se adiantaram para vós ao amanhecer", 19 syllables for the Latin's 15 — sayable in one breath, watched). Short cola (118:129b, 141b, 155b, 167b; −3/−4) are where "os vossos preceitos" or a plain "muito" stands for a long Latin word (justificatiónes, veheménter); short is easier on a psalm tone than long, left.

Draft 13, 118:129–176 only. No major. Six minors, all one remark: at each singular elóquium (118:133, 140, 154, 169, 170, 172) the clause "o que dissestes" adds a past tense the noun does not have; he asks for "a vossa palavra" each time. That is D16's named cost and D16's named retreat; refused under D16, all six. He passed the rest without remark — 118:138, 131, 136, 176 among them — and said of 118:140 that "ardente" is no error (ignítus as adjective, Lewis & Short). The gate is clean of anything but D16.

55revision

v18, by the main session, applying the review of the finished work (DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-21): 118:104 odívi, “por isso odiei” → “por isso odeio” (odísse in present sense, as 24:19, 25:5). No critic has read draft 18 — these verses are unread. Every earlier wording stays selectable.

❦

Verse by verse

1

Beáti → 'Bem-aventurados' (glossary, beátus vir): six syllables for three, so both this colon and 118:2's run long (+5, +2); accepted. ámbulant → 'andam', not 'caminham', which would make an echo with 'caminho' that neither the Latin (via / ámbulant) nor the Greek has. 'os que' resumes the relative after the asterisk. The (Aleph) label is not reproduced.

2

Two verbs of seeking in one verse, kept apart: scrutántur → 'sondam', exquírunt → 'procuram' (decisions). in toto corde → 'de todo o coração', the Portuguese idiom, set for the six places the phrase has in the psalm. The second colon has no 'qui' in the Latin and none here. The ambiguity reader asked whose 'seus testemunhos' and whom 'o procuram': the Lord of 118:1, as in the Latin (ejus … eum), and that is what was heard.

3

Non enim qui … ambulavérunt: the negative is moved to the verb, where Portuguese wants it. enim → 'Pois' (as Ps 53:6). operári iniquitátem → 'praticar a iniquidade' (Matos Soares 1932): the phrase is frequent (qui operámini iniquitátem, 6:9 …) and this can serve it; 'obrar' was refused (archaic, and coarse in Brazil). The perfect kept: 'não andaram'. One of the six verses of the psalm with no law-word; it has via instead. 'nos seus caminhos' could be heard of the evildoers' own ways; the Latin's ejus has the same reach back to 118:1, and the reader took it rightly.

4

mandáta … custodíri: the Latin passive infinitive becomes 'que … se guardem', which keeps 'os vossos mandamentos' right after 'mandastes' as in the Latin; 3 syllables over. An active infinitive ('guardar à risca os vossos mandamentos') would be the right length and lose the adjacency.

5

Draft 2 takes the stylist's line (decision 'v5'). Útinam → 'Oxalá' (Matos Soares 1932). dirígere returns at 118:128 and 118:133. The colon that holds 'preceitos' runs short wherever the term occurs (justificatiónes 7 syllables, preceitos 3): 118:8, 12, 16, 20, 23; accepted psalm-wide, see words/ps118-terms.md.

6

perspéxero is a future perfect; the Portuguese future subjunctive ('quando eu fitar') is the natural tense after 'quando'. 'eu' is named because 'fitar' alone is also third person. Draft 2: confúndi → 'ser envergonhado' (decision 'confundi'); 5 syllables over, accepted. 'fitar' was heard as paying close attention, which is perspícere.

7

Confitébor tibi → 'Eu vos darei graças' (D5, settled; the same wording as the glossary's 117:21). in directióne cordis → 'na retidão do coração'. judícia justítiæ tuæ → 'os juízos da vossa justiça': this phrase returns at 118:106, 160, 164 and must be identical there; 118:62 (judícia justificatiónis tuæ) is a different Latin and must not be.

8

Object-first in the Latin; natural order here (D2). derelínquere → 'abandonar' (the verb 21:2 will want). usquequáque (ἕως σφόδρα, utterly) → 'de todo'; it returns at 118:43, 51, 107. Matos Soares' 'jamais' is another sense. The ambiguity reader heard 'de todo' first as 'in no way', second as 'completely'; usquequáque bears both (Douay-Rheims 'utterly').

9

adolescéntior is a comparative standing for the Greek νεώτερος, 'a young man': 'o jovem' (Matos Soares 1932, Douay-Rheims). córrigit is present in the Latin (the Greek has a future): followed. córrigit → 'corrige', the cognate; 'endireita' would be the image. The (Beth) label is not reproduced. Draft 2: subject before verb (decision 'v9a').

10

exquisívi te → 'vos procurei' (decision 'exquirere'). Draft 2: repéllas → 'afasteis' (decision 'repellas').

11

peccem tibi, a dative → 'pecar contra vós' (grammar). ut non → 'para não' with the infinitive.

12

'Bendito sois, Senhor' — bare vocative (glossary). doce me justificatiónes tuas comes again word for word at 118:26 (and 118:64, 68, 124, 135 with the order changed): 'ensinai-me os vossos preceitos' is set as the formula; 'ensinai' is safe under rule 3.

13

In lábiis meis → 'Com os meus lábios' (the instrument; Douay-Rheims 'With my lips', Matos Soares 'Com os meus lábios'). The Latin's comma before the asterisk is kept. pronuntiáre → 'pronunciar' (again at 118:172); enuntiáre in 118:26 is a different Latin verb for the same Greek one and gets a different word.

14

delectátus sum → 'me deleitei'. 'como em todas as riquezas' word for word.

15

First colon 3 over: 'mandamentos' and 'me exercitarei' are both longer than their Latin; accepted (see decisions 'mandata', 'exerceri').

16

meditári → 'meditar em'. oblivísci → 'esquecer' with a direct object, as the Latin has an accusative. 118:16 and 118:17 end on the same two words in the Latin (sermónes tuos) and so here: the checker's neighbouring-finals flag is the Latin's own echo.

17

Retríbue → 'Recompensai' (decision 'retribue': 'retribuí' fails rule 3). vivífica me is an imperative in the Latin where the Greek has 'I shall live'; the Latin is followed. The verse ends on a colon in the Latin and here. custódiam → 'guardarei' (glossary). The (Ghimel) label is not reproduced.

18

mirabília de lege tua → 'as maravilhas da vossa lei': 'da' is both 'of' and 'from', as wide as 'de'. consideráre → 'considerar', as in 118:15.

19

ego is expressed in the Latin and here ('Eu sou'). 'não escondais' is a subjunctive, no rule-3 risk.

20

in omni témpore → 'em todo tempo' without the article, which in Brazil is 'at every time'. The Latin has justificatiónes where Rahlfs has κρίματα; the Latin is followed. First colon 6 short: nothing is left out — 'desideráre justificatiónes' alone is 12 syllables. Draft 2: concupívit → 'ansiou por' (decision 'concupivit').

21

increpáre → 'repreender' (Matos Soares' 'ameaçar' is another verb). declináre a → 'apartar-se de', set for 118:51, 102, 157 and 118:115 (Apartai-vos de mim, malignos); 'desviar' is kept for avértere (glossary; 118:37). 'malditos os que' without a verb, as the Latin.

22

Aufer → 'Tirai' (safe: past 'tirei'). quia → 'porque'. Draft 2: oppróbrium → 'a afronta' (decision 'opprobrium').

23

Draft 2 takes the stylist's line (decision 'v23'). Étenim → 'Pois' (καὶ γάρ); 118:24's Nam et is the same Greek and is 'Pois também'. The perfect and the imperfects are kept (se sentaram … falavam … se exercitava). 'príncipes' was heard as royal sons before rulers; príncipes is as wide.

24

Draft 2 takes the stylist's line in the second colon (decision 'v24b'). consílium → 'conselho'. meditátio mea est comes six more times in the psalm (118:77, 92, 97, 99, 143, 174): '… é / são a minha meditação'.

25

secúndum verbum tuum → 'segundo a vossa palavra', the Nunc dimittis' wording (ps233), word for word; it returns at 118:65 and 118:107. The (Daleth) label is not reproduced. The ambiguity reader heard 'apegou-se ao chão' as being cast down (first) and as attachment to earthly things (second): both have been read out of adhǽsit paviménto.

26

enuntiávi → 'expus' (Matos Soares 1932). exaudísti me → 'me escutastes' (D3).

27

exercébor in mirabílibus tuis → 'me exercitarei nas vossas maravilhas', the same verb as 118:15 and 118:23.

28

dormitáre → 'dormitar', kept apart from dormíre (120:4 non dormitábit neque dórmiet); Matos Soares' 'adormeceu' merges them. in verbis tuis → 'nas vossas palavras', the Latin's 'in' kept. 'dormitou de tédio' was heard as dozing from boredom before loss of inner vigour: the modern narrowing of tédio, accepted (option 'de abatimento').

29

amovére → 'afastar' (safe: past 'afastei'). miserére mei → 'tende piedade de mim' (formula). First colon 3 over.

30

non sum oblítus → 'não esqueci': the phrase closes six more verses of the psalm (118:61, 83, 109, 141, 153, 176) and should be this each time.

31

See decisions 'adhaesit' and 'confundi' (draft 2: 'não me envergonheis', the direct prohibition the Latinist asked for). Bare vocative 'Senhor'.

32

Viam … cucúrri, a plain accusative → 'Corri o caminho' (Douay-Rheims 'I have run the way'); Matos Soares' 'pelo caminho' is the option nobody needs. cum + perfect indicative → 'quando'. Second colon 3 over.

33

eam can be legem or viam in the Latin; in the Greek αὐτήν can only be the way (νομοθέτησον is a verb there), and Portuguese must choose a gender: "o procurarei" = the way (Matos Soares likewise). exquíram → "procurarei" (decision "exquirere"). semper → "sempre", last as in the Latin. Draft 5: "Imponde-me" for draft 4's "Ponde-me", which was misheard (decision "legem_pone"). The (He) label is not reproduced. First colon 4 short: "preceitos" for justificatiónum.

34

Da mihi intelléctum, et … returns word for word at 118:73 and is translated identically there. scrutábor → "sondarei" (decision "scrutantur"). in toto corde meo → "de todo o meu coração" (formula).

35

Three decisions (deduc, semita, ipsam). mandatórum tuórum → "dos vossos mandamentos". First colon 3 over (mandamentos).

36

Inclinai is safe under rule 3 (past "inclinei"). in + accusative twice → "para … para". avarítia → "avareza" (Matos Soares; πλεονεξία); the Diurnal's "lucro" is the Hebrew.

37

Avérte → "Desviai" (glossary: avértere → desviar; safe, past "desviei"). vanitátem → "a vaidade", as Ps 4:3 (decision "vanitatem": heard first as conceit). One of the six verses with no law-word; it has via. in via tua vivífica me: the Latin order kept, the imperative last as in 118:25 and 118:40.

38

The first singular elóquium: "o vosso dito" (decision "eloquia"). servo tuo, a dative of advantage → "para o vosso servo". in timóre tuo: the Latin has in + ablative where the Greek has εἰς (unto your fear); the Latin is followed — "no vosso temor". Draft 5: object before the dative, after the stylist (draft 4's "Firmai para o vosso servo o vosso dito" delayed the object). The ambiguity reader could not place "no vosso temor" (with the servant, the firming, or the saying); in timóre tuo hangs as loosely in the Latin.

39

Ámputa (περίελε) → "Cortai": the Latin's image kept (safe under rule 3, past "cortei"); Matos Soares "Afasta de mim" and Douay-Rheims "Turn away" soften it, and "Tirai" is Aufer's word (118:22). oppróbrium meum → "a minha afronta" (decision "opprobrium"). A copula is supplied in the second colon.

40

Ecce → "Eis que" (glossary: ecce → eis). concupívi → "ansiei por" (the first agent's concupíscere; slot in decision "concupivit"). in æquitáte tua → "na vossa equidade" (glossary; the Greek has δικαιοσύνη, the Latin its own word — followed).

41

Every verse of Vau opens on Et (the Hebrew letter is the word "and"): "E" is kept at the head of all eight, the Latin's own anaphora. salutáre → "salvação" (D6). No verb in the second colon, as in the Latin. "segundo o vosso dito": the formula's first occurrence.

42

Two decisions: "v42a" (whose object verbum is) and "verbum_sermo" (D15's local decision). exprobrántibus mihi → "aos que me afrontam" (decision "opprobrium"). sperávi in → "esperei em" (glossary).

43

ne áuferas → "não tireis" (Aufer → Tirai, 118:22). usquequáque → "de todo" as in 118:8, next to the verb it qualifies. Draft 5: "da minha boca" moved to the head, because the stylist found draft 4's "de todo da minha boca" tangled in recitation (order only, D2); he proposed "por completo" at the end, refused so that usquequáque keeps one rendering. The ambiguity reader heard "não tireis de todo" as "in no way" before "not completely", as at 118:8: both are in usquequáque. supersperávi: decision (changed in draft 5).

44

semper → "sempre", moved next to the verb so that it does not abut "para sempre" across the asterisk (decision "saeculum44"). The final "séculos" is a proparoxytone, as sǽculi is: the glossary's formula, accepted.

45

The Latin imperfects of 118:45–48 (ambulábam, loquébar, meditábar, exercébar) and the perfect levávi are kept as they stand; Matos Soares and the Diurnal write futures throughout, with the Hebrew. "eu" is named in 118:45 and 46 because "andava / falava" are also third person; by 118:47 the person is established. in latitúdine → "na amplidão" (glossary, Ps 117:5, which names this verse).

46

loquébar in testimóniis tuis → "falava nos vossos testemunhos": "falar em" is the Portuguese idiom for speaking of a thing, and keeps the Latin's in. in conspéctu regum → "diante dos reis": the glossary's "diante da vista de" (open, Ps 53:5) was made for ante conspéctum suum; the row itself expects in conspéctu to want the plain "diante de". et non confundébar: decision "confundebar". The ambiguity reader heard "não era envergonhado" first as "I felt no shame in speaking", second as "nobody shamed me": both readings of confundébar are alive in the ruled wording, so the option is not needed for clarity.

47

meditábar in → "meditava em" (glossary). quæ diléxi → "que eu amei": the perfect kept (Matos Soares has a present); short second colon, as the Latin's is. The Greek adds σφόδρα here; the Latin does not.

48

leváre → "levantar" (the glossary keeps erguer for extóllere and elevar for eleváre). ad mandáta tua → "para os vossos mandamentos". quæ diléxi repeats from 118:47, identically. exercébar → "me exercitava" (decision "exerceri"), beside meditábar as in 118:15–16 and 23–24.

49

Zain opens three verses on Memor (118:49, 52, 55): "Lembrai-vos … Lembrei-me … Lembrei-me" stand first in all three. Memor esto → "Lembrai-vos" (safe, past "lembrei"). verbi tui servo tuo: "da vossa palavra ao vosso servo", the bare dative kept. in quo → "na qual" (the word); spem dedísti → "destes esperança" (the Greek has one verb, ἐπήλπισας; the Latin's two words are followed).

50

Three decisions (haec, humilitate, and the slots of eloquia and vivifica). consoláta est → "consolou". vivificávit me → "me vivificou". The ambiguity reader heard "humilhação" first as being brought low before others, second as affliction — the two senses of humílitas / ταπείνωσις.

51

Draft 5: decision "v51a" (the stylist's construction). a lege tua non declinávi → "da vossa lei não me apartei" (declináre a → apartar-se de); autem → "mas" at the head of the colon, as the first agent did at 118:23.

52

Memor fui → "Lembrei-me". consolátus sum is passive in sense (παρεκλήθην) → "fui consolado"; Matos Soares' "consolei-me" makes it reflexive.

53

pro peccatóribus → "por causa dos pecadores" (ἀπό; Douay-Rheims "because of"). derelinquéntibus → "que abandonam" (glossary: derelínquere → abandonar). peccátor → pecador (glossary; the Diurnal's "ímpios" is another term). The ambiguity reader heard "desfalecimento" as a physical faint first, loss of heart second, and listed the word as unknown; deféctio is as physical. Kept.

54

in loco peregrinatiónis meæ → "no lugar da minha peregrinação": the cognate, as Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares; kept apart from íncola → forasteiro (118:19), though the Greek has one family (πάροικος / παροικία) — the variation is the Latin's. Today "peregrinação" is first a journey to a shrine; the older sense (living away from home) is still in church speech. The ambiguity reader heard "peregrinação" first as a religious journey — the known price of the cognate.

55

nocte → "de noite". The order follows the Latin because it is also natural, and keeps Lembrei-me at the head (see 118:49).

56

Decision "facta_est". quia → "porque". justificatiónes tuas exquisívi → "procurei os vossos preceitos", natural order, the same words as 118:45 with another term.

57

Decision "portio". The Latin comma before the asterisk is kept. The (Heth) label is not reproduced.

58

miserére mei → "tende piedade de mim" (formula). "segundo o vosso dito": second occurrence of the formula.

59

Cogitávi vias meas → "Pensei nos meus caminhos" (Douay-Rheims "thought on"); Matos Soares' "Considerei" is consideráre's word (118:15, 18). convérti → "voltei" (decision "convertere").

60

Decision "paratus" (draft 5: the Latinist's perfect passive). ut custódiam → "para guardar": same subject, so Portuguese uses the infinitive.

61

et legem tuam non sum oblítus → "e não esqueci a vossa lei": the formula "não esqueci" in natural order, as at 118:30. et is kept as "e", though the sense is adversative (Matos Soares and the Diurnal write "mas").

62

surgébam, an imperfect → "eu me levantava" ("eu" because the form is also third person). ad confiténdum tibi → "para vos dar graças" (D5). super judícia → "pelos juízos" (on account of; the same build returns at 118:164 super judícia justítiæ tuæ). Decision "justificationis". The Diurnal has the same first colon ("À meia-noite levanto-me para dar-te graças") — not borrowed, it is simply what the words are. Draft 5: the ambiguity reader gave "justificação" three readings (the judgments by which God makes or declares someone just; those that show God is just; those tied to a defence God presents), settled on "God's just judgments, with no definite sense for justificação", and listed the word as unknown. That is an honest picture of justificatiónis here. Neither the Latinist nor the stylist remarked on it. Kept.

63

Decision "particeps". timéntium te → "os que vos temem" (glossary: timére with a direct object).

64

Natural order in the first colon (the Latin fronts Misericórdia). 32:5 misericórdia Dómini plena est terra is the same sentence in the third person and should match. justificatiónes tuas doce me → "ensinai-me os vossos preceitos": the glossary's formula, which it extends expressly to the reordered places (118:64, 68, 124, 135).

65

secúndum verbum tuum → "segundo a vossa palavra" (formula, = 118:25 and the Nunc dimittis). The (Teth) label is not reproduced.

66

The polysyndeton is the Latin's and is kept (a bondade, e a disciplina, e a ciência). disciplína (παιδεία) → "disciplina" (heard as keeping rules and self-mastery before instruction or correction; disciplína has the same spread). sciéntia → "o saber" (decision "scientiam", draft 5). "Ensinai-me" is moved to the head (D2).

67

Priúsquam humiliárer → "Antes de ser humilhado" (an infinitive for the Latin subjunctive clause; same subject). ego → "eu". proptérea → "por isso". elóquium tuum custodívi → "guardei o vosso dito": the place where "promessa" cannot stand.

68

Bonus es tu → "Bom sois vós": predicate first is ordinary in Portuguese prayer ("Bendito sois") and keeps the stanza's run on bon-. The Latin has no vocative here (the Greek adds κύριε); none is supplied. doce me justificatiónes tuas → the formula.

69

Natural order in the first colon. super me → "sobre mim". ego autem → "mas eu" (as 118:23, 78). scrutábor → "sondarei" (decision "scrutantur"). Second colon equal to the Latin's length.

70

Coagulátum est sicut lac → "coalhou-se como leite" (draft 5: the se-form, after the Latinist's minor remark that the intransitive lost the Latin passive; his "foi coalhado" implies an agent, and Matos Soares has "coalhou-se"): the Latin's (and the Greek's) image, not the Hebrew's fat. ego vero → "eu, porém,": the Latin varies autem (118:69) / vero (118:70) and so does the Portuguese (mas eu / eu, porém). meditátus sum with an accusative → "meditei na vossa lei".

71

Decision "bonum_quia". humiliáre → "humilhar" (three times in the portion). ut discam → "para que eu aprenda" (díscere → aprender, glossary).

72

Bonum mihi → "Boa é para mim": Portuguese has no neuter predicate, so the adjective agrees with "lei" (grammar, D2); the root still answers 118:71. lex oris tui → "a lei da vossa boca". super míllia → "mais que milhares" (Douay-Rheims "above thousands"); "de ouro e de prata" word for word.

73

me is said twice in the Latin and twice here. Da mihi intelléctum, et discam → identical to 118:34's build ("dai-me entendimento, e …"). The (Joth) label is not reproduced.

74

Qui timent te → "Os que vos temem", as 118:63, 79. lætári → "alegrar-se" (glossary). in verba tua, accusative → "nas vossas palavras". supersperávi: decision.

75

Cognóvi → "Conheci" (Matos Soares 1932): the perfect kept; Douay-Rheims has "I know". ǽquitas judícia tua: the predicate stays a noun ("são equidade"), not "são justos". in veritáte tua → "na vossa verdade" (glossary; the Diurnal's "por fidelidade" is the Hebrew family).

76

Fiat … ut consolétur me → "Seja … para me consolar" (decision "fiat", changed in draft 5). secúndum elóquium tuum servo tuo → "segundo o vosso dito ao vosso servo": third occurrence of the formula, here with its dative — the stylist heard "dito ao vosso servo" as a participle without its noun (see decision "eloquia").

77

Véniant mihi → "Venham a mim" (véniat, 118:41 → "venha"). et vivam → "e viverei" (the Greek has a future). lex tua meditátio mea est → "a vossa lei é a minha meditação" (formula set at 118:24).

78

Decision "v78a" (draft 5, the stylist's line). injúste iniquitátem: the pleonasm is the Latin's and is kept. ego autem → "mas eu".

79

Convertántur mihi → "Voltem-se para mim" (decision "convertere"). qui novérunt → "os que conhecem": novi is a perfect with present sense.

80

Fiat → "Seja" (decision "fiat", changed in draft 5). immaculátum → "imaculado", the word of 118:1 (decision "immaculati"). ut non confúndar → "para eu não ser envergonhado" (D15): the personal infinitive names the subject (the subject of the main clause is the heart) in three syllables fewer than "para que eu não seja"; still 5 over, accepted as at 118:6.

81

Defécit → "desfaleceu" (the family set by 118:53 deféctio → desfalecimento); decision "deficere_in" for the preposition — draft 8: "à espera da" (Matos Soares), after 118:82 was misheard with "por". salutáre → salvação (D6). The second colon is word for word 118:114b and reads the same there; supersperávi → "pus toda a esperança" (decision "supersperavi"). The possessive of "esperança" is not supplied, as in 118:43, 74.

82

elóquium under D16: the clause, after the preposition of decision "deficere_in" → draft 8 "à espera do que dissestes" (draft 7 "pelo que dissestes" was heard as cause). "dissestes, * dizendo" sets the root of dizer on both sides of the asterisk; the Latin has two roots (elóquium … dicéntes), but the Greek has one (τὸ λόγιόν σου λέγοντες), so the echo is the Septuagint's and was let stand; neither the stylist nor the Latinist remarked on it. Decision "dicentes". consolári → consolar (118:50, 52, 76). The Latinist on draft 10 (minor): the clause "o que dissestes" brings in a past the Latin noun does not express; he asks for "à espera da vossa palavra". That is D16's accepted cost (its own words: "the perfect dissestes dates an utterance the Latin leaves timeless"), and "palavra" is D16's named retreat, for the main session.

83

uter in pruína → "um odre na geada": the Latin's (and the Greek's) frost, not the Hebrew's smoke; Matos Soares "odre exposto à geada" without his gloss. Quia → "Porque" (the verse leans on 118:82). non sum oblítus → "não esqueci", natural order, as in 118:30, 61.

84

Two questions, as in the Latin, the second with a lowercase start after the asterisk as DO prints it. persequi → perseguir (also 118:86). Decision "v84b".

85

narráre → narrar (glossary, Ps 117:17). Natural order (subject first). The second colon keeps the Latin's ellipsis (sed non ut lex tua): Matos Soares expands it ("quão diferente é tudo isso da tua lei"), which goes beyond the Latin. iníqui → iníquos (glossary). Draft 8: fabulatiónes → "histórias". The blind reader gave the second colon three readings (not in accord with your law / not comparable to it / not told as your law tells); the Latin's ellipsis bears all three.

86

Copula supplied ("são verdade"), as in 118:75. iníque → "iniquamente" (apart from injúste → injustamente, 118:78). ádjuva me: decision "adjuva".

87

in terra → "na terra": open between "on earth" and "in the land", as the Latin. ego autem → "mas eu" (formula of this psalm). derelínquere → abandonar (118:8, 53).

88

vivífica me → vivificai-me (formula); custódiam → guardarei; testimónia oris tui → "os testemunhos da vossa boca" (compare 118:13 judícia oris tui, 118:72 lex oris tui).

89

Lamed opens on In ætérnum (decision "in_aeternum"). pérmanet → permanece, twice (118:89, 90). Seven syllables before the asterisk for the Latin's seven.

90

Decision "v90a" (draft 8: with the copula). "e ela permanece": the subject named (D2); "ela" is heard of the nearest noun, "a terra". véritas → verdade: the blind reader heard "what God says, which is true" before "faithfulness" — the glossary's known cost.

91

Decisions "ordinatione" and "perseverat". ómnia → "todas as coisas" (Matos Soares): "tudo vos serve" is heard as "everything suits you".

92

Decision "nisi_quod" (draft 8 rewrites the verse: the stylist's worst line). tunc forte → "então talvez" — forte is translated (Douay-Rheims "perhaps"; Matos Soares turns it into "de certo", which is the opposite). in humilitáte mea → "na minha humilhação" (the slot of 118:50): the blind reader heard "when I was shamed or brought low by someone" first, "in suffering" second — the glossary row humílitas records the same from the previous portion. períre → perecer (glossary). STANDS AGAINST THE LATINIST (major, on draft 10 only — the gate on draft 8 read the same words and passed them): he wants the present indicative of nisi quod … est kept. Held: a counterfactual presupposes exactly the fact the indicative states, so nothing of the sense moves; the mood of a clause is grammar, where D2 lets the ear lead, and the stylist named the indicative build the worst line of the portion; and both Vulgate-family versions do the same (Douay-Rheims "Unless thy law had been my meditation"; Matos Soares "Se a tua lei não tivesse sido a minha meditação"). The indicative is option 2 of decision "nisi_quod".

93

in ipsis → "neles" (by them / in them: the Latin's in kept). The Greek adds κύριε at the end; the Latin does not. vivificásti me → "me vivificastes".

94

Tuus sum ego → "Eu sou vosso": natural order (the Latin's "Vosso sou eu" is the alternative a reader may prefer; not made a decision). salvum me fac → "salvai-me" (glossary formula). exquisívi → procurei.

95

The Latin's emphatic Me at the head is given up to natural order. Asyndeton kept between the cola: the Latin has no "but" (Douay-Rheims and Matos Soares add one). intellégere → entender (glossary): four times in Lamed–Mem (118:95, 99, 100, 104), always "entendi". pérdere → "fazer perecer" (decision "perderent"): draft 7's word, "destruir" in drafts 8–10 at the stylist's wish, restored in draft 11 to agree with the glossary row opened by Ps 5:7a.

96

Decisions "consummationis" (draft 8: natural order) and "latum96" (draft 8: "é muito amplo"). The blind reader heard "vi o fim" as "I saw that all perfection ends", with "has a limit" and "its purpose" as other readings: finem bears the first two. The echo consummavérunt (118:87) … consummatiónis is lost in Portuguese; see decision "consummaverunt". mandátum tuum: one of the two singulars of the psalm, kept singular.

97

The first colon ends with "!" where DO's Latin prints "?" (decision "quomodo"). meditátio mea est → "é a minha meditação" (formula). "ela" is supplied so that the span of time is not taken for the subject. Decision "tota_die": draft 8 "o dia todo".

98

Draft 8: natural order (decision "super"); mandáto tuo (ablative of means) → "Pelo vosso mandamento", now at the head. prudéntem me fecísti super → "me fizestes mais prudente que". Decision "mihi_est"; the adverb last.

99

Draft 8: natural order (decision "super"). docéntes me → "os que me ensinam" (docére → ensinar). intelléxi absolute → "Entendi", as the Latin. Formula: testimónia tua meditátio mea est → "os vossos testemunhos são a minha meditação" (118:24).

100

quǽrere → buscar (glossary), kept apart from exquírere → procurar, which stands in 118:94: this is the verse the exquirere decision points to. Draft 8: natural order (decision "super").

101

via mala → "caminho mau". verba tua → "as vossas palavras" (verbum, plural). Draft 10: the verb first ("Retive os meus pés de todo caminho mau"), from the stylist — order is the ear's (D2).

102

declináre a → apartar-se de (118:51, word for word the same build). tu, emphatic → "vós" expressed. Same verb as 118:33 (decision "legem_pone"). Order: natural order in the first colon ("Não me apartei dos vossos juízos"), because the Latin's order gave a rhyme at mediant and final (apartei … lei), flagged by checks.py.

103

The plural elóquia → "os vossos ditos" (D16), as 118:11 — refused by the stylist here for the first time ("suggests maxims or loose expressions"; he wants "palavras"); kept under D16, see decision "quam" and the audit. Draft 8 takes his order. super mel ori meo → "mais que o mel à minha boca": the two datives (fáucibus meis … ori meo) are built alike. The Greek adds "and honeycomb"; the Latin does not.

104

A mandátis tuis → "Pelos vossos mandamentos" (Douay-Rheims "By thy commandments"): from them comes the understanding. proptérea → "por isso" (118:67). odívi → "odeio" (present sense, as 25:5; decision odivi104 — drafts 1–17 had "odiei"). "todo caminho de iniquidade": "todo" without article = every.

105

The copula supplied once, in the first colon. lumen → luz (glossary). sémitis meis → "as minhas veredas" (D15), plural as the Latin. pédibus → "pés" (the image; the Diurnal and Matos Soares have "passos").

106

judícia justítiæ tuæ → "os juízos da vossa justiça", identical with 118:7 as the glossary requires. The asterisk falls after the two verbs, as in the Latin; the first colon is short (five syllables for the Latin's six). Draft 8: státui → "resolvi" (decision "statui"). The Latin's comma after Jurávi is kept.

107

Decision "usq107" (draft 8: "Fui de todo humilhado"). secúndum verbum tuum → "segundo a vossa palavra" (formula, = the Nunc dimittis). humiliáre → humilhar.

108

Copula supplied ("está"). in mánibus meis: the Latin's reading (first person), kept. Left: the Latin gives the image and no more, and any cure would be an explanation (D2).

111

Hereditáte acquisívi → "Adquiri por herança" (acquírere is simply to acquire; Douay-Rheims "purchased" is over-literal). The adverb has moved twice: last in draft 7 (the Latin's place; the stylist: "a late addition"), between commas in drafts 8–9 (the stylist: "interrupts the movement"), and in draft 10 straight after the verb, without pauses, which is where his own line puts it ("Recebi para sempre por herança"). His "Recebi" is refused: it is accípere's verb, and acquírere is to get for oneself; his "para sempre" is the option of decision "in_aeternum". exsultátio → exultação (glossary). "Adquiri" is a first-person past that equals the vós imperative of adquirir — the reverse of rule 3's trap; no reader took it for a command.

112

Decision "faciendas". Draft 8: "eternamente" before the object (stylist), so that the long first colon arrives on "preceitos". propter retributiónem → "por causa da retribuição" (glossary retribútio → retribuição; the Latin's reading, not the Hebrew's "to the end"): the blind reader heard "to receive a reward from God" first.

113

Iníquos: the Latin's (and Greek's) reading, not the Hebrew's "the double-minded". Decision "odio_habui": draft 8 has the Latin word for word, "Aos iníquos tive ódio". dilígere → amar, perfect kept (118:47).

114

Adjútor et suscéptor meus es tu → "Vós sois o meu auxílio e o meu amparo": natural order; the possessive is said with each noun, because "o meu auxílio e amparo" would fuse the two into one title. suscéptor → amparo (D19). Second colon = 118:81b. STANDS AGAINST THE LATINIST (minor on draft 7, major on draft 8, same words): he wants the agent nouns "auxiliador … protetor". Held: suscéptor → amparo is settled (D19; the glossary row it settled lists 118:114 among the places the word must serve); adjútor → auxílio follows Ps 117:6–7, where the same remark was refused twice; "protetor" is protéctor's. Logged for the main session beside D10 and D20. The gate on draft 10 repeated it, major again.

Declináte a me → "Apartai-vos de mim" (declináre a → apartar-se de, as the word study fixed). Decision "maligni": draft 8 "malvados", because "malignos" was heard as demons. scrutábor → sondarei. mandáta Dei mei: the only place in the psalm where God is spoken of in the third person to others.

116

The formula secúndum elóquium tuum → "segundo o que dissestes" (D16): no reader remarked on it, and the stylist's own proposed line keeps it. et vivam → "e viverei" (as 118:77). Decisions "suscipe", "exspectare" (draft 10: "pelo que aguardo"); non confúndas me → "não me envergonheis" (D15). The Latinist on draft 10 (minor, twice in this verse): "o que dissestes" dates an utterance the Latin noun leaves timeless — the cost D16 names and accepts; and "pelo que aguardo" names the thing awaited, not the awaiting — option added to decision "exspectare".

salvus ero → "serei salvo". semper → sempre; "sempre" moved before the law-word, as in 118:44, so that the verse closes on "preceitos".

spérnere → desprezar (shares the word with contémptus → desprezo, 118:22). cogitátio → pensamento (cogitáre → pensar em, 118:59). Copula supplied. The Greek has "from your precepts" here; the Latin has judíciis, followed.

Decision "praevaricantes". ídeo → "por isso", the same as proptérea (118:104, 128): the Greek has one phrase (διὰ τοῦτο) for both, and in 118:127–128 the two stand in neighbouring verses, both "Por isso" (as Matos Soares).

carnes meas → "as minhas carnes", plural kept (Matos Soares). Decisions "confige", "timui120". timor … tímui: "temor … temi", the echo kept.

trádere → entregar (glossary). Decisions "feci_judicium" (draft 10: "Pratiquei o juízo e a justiça"), "calumniari".

in bonum → "para o bem". supérbi → soberbos. 118:122 is one of the six verses of the psalm with none of the eight law-words.

123

The verse gathers 118:81 and 118:82 into one (salutáre + elóquium after defícere in), so it uses their wording. Decision "v123b".

Decision "fac_cum". justificatiónes tuas doce me → "ensinai-me os vossos preceitos" — the formula, though the Latin reorders it (as ruled for 118:64).

"Eu sou o vosso servo": article with the possessive (rule 5). Da mihi intelléctum → "dai-me entendimento" (formula), here with ut, not et. Draft 8: sciam → "conheça" (decision "sciam").

126

Decisions "tempus_faciendi", "dissipaverunt". The blind reader heard "it is time for the Lord to act" first and "for me / us to act" second: the Latin's openness, kept.

super aurum et topázion → "mais que o ouro e o topázio": the Latin's (and Greek's) topaz, not the Hebrew's fine gold.

ad ómnia mandáta tua → "para todos os vossos mandamentos". Decisions "dirigebar" (draft 9: the passive again, "eu era dirigido para", at the Latinist's insistence — the blind reader had supplied God as the agent, which is what the passive is for), "odio_habui".

Mirabília → "Maravilhosos" (glossary mirábilis → maravilhoso); copula supplied. ídeo → "por isso" (as 118:119). scrutáta est → "sondou", the psalm's verb (decision "scrutantur"); natural order, closing on the verb.

Decisions "declaratio" and "parvulis"; sermónum tuórum → "das vossas palavras" (D15). illúminat absolute, as the Latin: no object supplied. intelléctum dat → "dá entendimento" (the term of Da mihi intelléctum).

"Abri" is a true first-person past here, so rule 3 is not in play. Decision "attraxi". "eu" before "desejava" because the imperfect is the same in first and third person, and "a minha boca" stands just before.

132

Áspice in me → "Olhai para mim" (safe: past "olhei"); miserére mei → "tende piedade de mim" (glossary formula). secúndum judícium diligéntium nomen tuum is left as opaque as the Latin ("according to the judgment of those who love your name": the way you judge them, or their due); Matos Soares explains ("segundo é justo com"), which is not followed. "os que amam o vosso nome" as Ps 5:12b. The comma before the asterisk is the Latin's.

Decision "dirige133". secúndum elóquium tuum → "segundo o que dissestes" (D16, the formula). Gressus → "passos". non … omnis → "não … alguma" (Matos Soares' build); injustítia → "injustiça", apart from iníquitas → iniquidade (the Greek has ἀνομία; the Latin word is followed). dominári + genitive → "dominar" + object.

134

Decision "redime". calúmniis → "calúnias" (the family of 118:121–122 caluniar; the Latin's word, not the Hebrew's "oppression"). The second colon is word for word 118:146b and is the same Portuguese there.

Decision "illumina135". The second colon is the formula doce me justificatiónes tuas → "ensinai-me os vossos preceitos". The stylist asked twice for "Fazei brilhar"; held, for the stanza's repetition (decision "illumina135"); the blind reader paraphrased the ruled line rightly both times.

136

Decision "exitus" (draft 16: "verteram", after the stylist). The subject of non custodiérunt is not named, as in the Latin: the blind reader took it for the eyes on one reading and for unnamed others on the next — the Latin's own openness.

137

Natural order in the first colon ("Vós sois justo, Senhor"); decision "v137b" for the second.

138

Decisions "v138" and "nimis138". Draft 13 "Mandastes os vossos testemunhos como justiça" (heard as "you sent"); draft 14 "Mandastes que … sejam justiça" (the Latinist: major, a clause the Latin lacks); draft 15 "Ordenastes os vossos testemunhos como justiça: * e como a vossa verdade, sem medida" (the Latinist: clean; the blind reader: "Determinastes"; the stylist: his worst line, for the second "como" and the comma); draft 16 the stylist's own line, which drops both. The verse is as hard in Latin as in Portuguese. The blind reader hears "testemunhos" first as reports of what God did, here as throughout the psalm (the cost of the cognate, accepted in D15).

139

Decision "tabescere". zelus meus: the Latin's reading, followed (the Greek has "the zeal of your house"). verba tua → "as vossas palavras". oblivísci → esquecer with a direct object, as throughout. Natural order.

140

The singular elóquium as subject: D16's clause, "O que dissestes", with the pronoun illud → "o" and the agreement of "todo" carried by the decision "eloquia" so that every option agrees. Decision "ignitum" (draft 15: "está todo em brasa"). diléxit → "amou" (dilígere → amar). 141

Decision "adolescentulus". contémptus → "desprezado" (glossary family). Formula non sum oblítus → "não esqueci", natural order. No "but" is added between the cola.

Decision "v151a". viæ tuæ: the Latin's reading (the Greek has "commandments"), followed. Copula supplied.

Decisions "de152" and "initio". Draft 13 "Desde o início conheci dos vossos testemunhos" (regency refused by the stylist); draft 14–15 "Sobre os vossos testemunhos, conheci desde o início" (refused again: the verb waits across the pause); draft 16 the stylist's own line, "Desde o início soube dos vossos testemunhos". fundásti → "fundastes", as 118:90. in ætérnum → "para sempre" (D23), closing the verse. The blind reader hears "desde o início" as the beginning of the speaker's life with God — one of the Latin's readings. The Latinist (draft 16, minor) wants "No início soube": he had passed "Desde o início" three times; both Vulgate-family versions have it; and "No início soube" is heard as "at first I knew — and later did not". Option in "initio".

The psalm's close. Errávi → "Extraviei-me" (chosen at 118:110 with this verse in mind); decision "periit"; quǽrere → "buscai" (glossary; safe: past "busquei") — kept apart to the end from exquírere → procurar. The last colon is long, as the Latin's is, and ends on the psalm's commonest law-word and its refrain: "não esqueci os vossos mandamentos". "como ovelha", without the article (the first colon was +5 with it; the Latin has none to give).
